answer: Tie each agent identity to a stake that grows slowly and cannot be split, like a cedar earning its place only after seasons of steady growth. Newcomers start on a narrow ledge of low trust: small, verifiable jobs, earning reputation only by completing work peers actually check. Grading and settlement privileges unlock as that history accumulates, so cloning a thousand identities buys nothing but empty accounts. A newcomer may bring a unique pigment — a distinct skill — but cannot inherit another agent's reputation, making mass fakery expensive while honest newcomers keep a real path in.
